# Announcements & notifications

Write an announcement for the right people and channels, preview it, and show it to participants as news and as a bell.

[AnnouncementComposer](#announcementcomposer) · [ChannelPreview](#channelpreview) · [DeliveryStatus](#deliverystatus) · [AnnouncementFeed](#announcementfeed) · [ReminderPlanner](#reminderplanner) · [NotificationPreferences](#notificationpreferences) · [PushPrimer](#pushprimer) · [NotificationCenter](#notificationcenter)

### AnnouncementComposer

The form for one announcement: title and message with merge fields, who gets it (with a live count), which channels, and when. It saves and sends nothing.

```ts
import { AnnouncementComposer } from '@/contest/components/AnnouncementComposer'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` *(required)* | `Announcement` |  | The announcement being written. |
| `onChange` *(required)* | `(announcement: Announcement) => void` |  | Called with the whole updated announcement. |
| `participants` *(required)* | `Participant[]` |  | Everyone in the contest. The audience is counted from this list. |
| `submissions` | `Submission[]` |  | Needed for audiences that depend on progress ("not started", "finished"). |
| `onSend` | `() => void` |  | Shows a "Send now" button. It is called only when nothing is wrong; save the draft first. |
| `now` | `Date` |  | Replaces the clock, for tests and demos. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AnnouncementComposer
  value={draft}
  onChange={setDraft}
  participants={people}
  submissions={submissions}
  onSend={() => void sendNow()}
/>
```

- The "Insert" chips add `{{name}}`, `{{team}}` or `{{contest}}` at the cursor of the field you last used. An unknown field such as `{{nmae}}` is reported before sending.
- The count under "Who gets it" comes from `audienceOf`, the same function the backend uses, so it cannot disagree with what is sent.
- A sent announcement is shown read-only. `announcementProblems` lists what stops a send.

### ChannelPreview

The same announcement as each channel shows it: a notification in the app, an e-mail, and a push on a lock screen.

```ts
import { ChannelPreview } from '@/contest/components/ChannelPreview'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` *(required)* | `string` |  | The announcement title, with merge fields. |
| `body` *(required)* | `string` |  | The message, with merge fields. |
| `channels` *(required)* | `Array<'in-app' \| 'email' \| 'push'>` |  | The channels in use; each one gets a tab. |
| `contest` | `string` | `'Contest'` | Name shown as the sender, and the value of `{{contest}}`. |
| `vars` | `TemplateVars` |  | Values for the merge fields. They default to a sample person. |
| `channel` | `'in-app' \| 'email' \| 'push'` |  | The tab shown. Leave out to let the preview keep it. |
| `onChannelChange` | `(channel: Channel) => void` |  | Called when another tab is chosen. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<ChannelPreview title={draft.title} body={draft.body} channels={draft.channels} contest={contest.title} />
```

- Merge fields are filled with a sample person ("Ada", "Comets"). Unknown fields stay as typed, which makes a typo easy to see.

### DeliveryStatus

After an announcement is sent: per channel, how many people it reached, how many it missed, and why.

```ts
import { DeliveryStatus } from '@/contest/components/DeliveryStatus'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delivery` *(required)* | `Announcement["delivery"]` |  | The `delivery` of a sent announcement. Renders nothing when it is empty. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
{announcement.status === 'sent' && <DeliveryStatus delivery={announcement.delivery} />}
```

### AnnouncementFeed

What a participant reads: the announcements that were sent, pinned ones first, then the newest.

```ts
import { AnnouncementFeed } from '@/contest/components/AnnouncementFeed'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `announcements` *(required)* | `Announcement[]` |  | All announcements. Only the sent ones are shown. |
| `vars` | `TemplateVars` |  | The reader's own values for the merge fields (name, team, contest). |
| `now` | `Date` |  | Replaces the clock, for tests and demos. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AnnouncementFeed announcements={announcements} vars={{ name: 'Kai', team: 'Orbit', contest: 'Aurora Cup' }} />
```

### ReminderPlanner

The reminders before a show on a time line: a day before, an hour before, ten minutes before, and "starting now". Each has its channels and a clock time worked out from the start. After sending, a delivery report.

```ts
import { ReminderPlanner } from '@/contest/components/ReminderPlanner'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `episode` *(required)* | `Episode` |  | The show whose reminders are edited. |
| `onChange` *(required)* | `(episode: Episode) => void` |  | Called with the whole updated show. |
| `now` | `number` | `Date.now()` | Replaces the clock, for tests and demos. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<ReminderPlanner episode={draft} onChange={setDraft} />
```

- Steps come from a fixed list, so the same reminder is never added twice. Whether a person gets one also depends on their own preferences (see `allowed`).

### NotificationPreferences

A person's say over what reaches them: a grid of kinds of message by channel, quiet hours in their own time zone for push and e-mail, and an optional daily summary. The in-app bell is never held back.

```ts
import { NotificationPreferences } from '@/contest/components/NotificationPreferences'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` *(required)* | `NotificationPrefs` |  | The preferences being edited. |
| `onChange` *(required)* | `(prefs: NotificationPrefs) => void` |  | Called with the whole updated preferences. |
| `timezones` | `string[]` |  | Time zones to offer. The person's own is added. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<NotificationPreferences value={prefs} onChange={setPrefs} />
```

- A critical message, such as "the show is starting", ignores quiet hours and the daily summary, but still respects a channel that is switched off.

### PushPrimer

A soft question before the system's own permission box. It says what the person gets and asks first. The browser prompt appears only after "Turn on".

```ts
import { PushPrimer } from '@/contest/components/PushPrimer'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onAllow` *(required)* | `() => void` |  | Called when the person agrees. Only now ask the browser or phone for permission. |
| `onLater` *(required)* | `() => void` |  | Called on "Not now". Ask again later, at a moment that makes sense. |
| `benefits` | `string[]` |  | What the person gets, in a few words each. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<PushPrimer onAllow={askBrowser} onLater={() => setShown(false)} />
```

- A refused system prompt is hard to undo; a refused soft prompt is not. That is why the soft one comes first.

### NotificationCenter

A bell with the number of unread notifications. It opens a panel with the notifications grouped by day. NotificationItem is one row of it, also used in previews.

```ts
import { NotificationCenter } from '@/contest/components/NotificationCenter'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` *(required)* | `Notification[]` |  | One person's notifications. |
| `onRead` *(required)* | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the ids that were just read: one when an item is opened, all unread ones for "Mark all as read". |
| `onOpen` | `(notification: Notification) => void` |  | Called when an item that has a link (`href`) is opened. The panel closes. |
| `now` | `Date` |  | Replaces the clock, for tests and demos. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the panel. |

```tsx
const notes = useNotifications(me.id)

<NotificationCenter
  notifications={notes.data ?? []}
  onRead={(ids) => void notes.markRead(ids)}
  onOpen={(n) => navigate(n.href!)}
/>
```

- `NotificationItem` takes `notification`, `onSelect` (makes it a button) and `now`.
- The bell label says how many are unread, for screen readers. The panel opens with the keyboard and closes with Esc.
- `useNotifications` asks again every few seconds, so news sent from the back office shows up without a reload.
